title: Senior WHS Manager
descriptionHtml:
The Sr. WHS (Workplace Health and Safety) Manager will be primarily responsible for managing all health and safety matters for our Quick Commerce sites and third-party operations. The individual will implement Amazon's safety policies and ensure compliance with all applicable local and regional regulations. Leveraging lean principles and kaizens, this individual will lead continuous improvement initiatives to reduce WHS risks in our processes, ensuring a safe and healthy working environment for associates and contractors.
The Sr. WHS Manager must demonstrate the ability to build trust and confidence with the Operations team, influencing change through comprehensive risk assessments and safety data analysis. The Sr. WHS Manager must be an effective communicator, delivering clear, concise, and consistent messages, both verbally and in writing. This individual will be responsible for instructing and training Operations leaders on company safety policies and assisting regional teams in incorporating safety standards at their sites.

The Sr. WHS Manager will identify best practices and incorporate them into standards to continuously improve company safety policies. This role requires excellent safety program knowledge and relevant safety, environmental, and ergonomic expertise, demonstrated through direct engagement with Operations. Additionally, the Sr. WHS Manager will support WHS activities and programs related to new expansions and launches in the region, ensuring that new projects are executed safely without delays due to safety concerns. This individual will work closely with Building Design, Launch, DCS, Legal, and Engineering teams to provide WHS assessments at different phases.

The Sr. WHS Manager will lead a team of WHS professionals responsible for auditing Quick Commerce sites and third-party sites. This individual must create and execute leadership development plans for team members, communicate expectations, provide frequent and appropriate feedback, and ensure the team is executing to the core competencies of an Amazon WHS professional. The Sr. WHS Manager must also demonstrate the ability to assess WHS talent and select appropriate bench strength to meet current and future business needs.


Key job responsibilities
1. Possess a thorough understanding of local and regional regulations and the ability to work with these alongside company policies.
2. Provide guidance and oversight to ensure compliance with all applicable Amazon WHS policies.
3. Measure the region and sites' performance against published requirements in WHS policies. For all deficiencies, identify and implement a plan to fix them.
4. Deliver quality projects on time to Operations.
5. Analyse WHS metrics and review weekly and monthly incident trends to justify the allocation of appropriate resources to areas where WHS risk is highest.
6. Analyse WHS review and audit results, and develop and implement solutions to eliminate exposure to these risks and prevent injuries at other facilities.
7. Audit workplace organization and associate behaviours to ensure that training, auditing, and scoring methods are accurate and consistent.
8. Manage and mentor the WHS team in assigned facilities.
9. Create scalable processes and mechanisms to ensure third-party operations comply with all local regulations.
10. Provide necessary training to the Operations team so that our third-party partners operate in a safe environment.
11. Lead injury reduction efforts by performing targeted kaizens in partnership with Operations teams based on risks identified in each task and at each job position.
12. Review the effectiveness of deployed WHS tools and revise them to ensure continual improvement.
13. Partner with corporate and other regional field WHS personnel to leverage global WHS best practices into Quick Commerce and third-party network standards.

Basic qualifications

- 10+ years of people leadership, or 7+ years of management experience
- Bachelor's degree in engineering or safety
- Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in safety and/or environmental programs within manufacturing, production, service operations, or other relevant settings applicable to the role

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in a fast paced, dynamic organization
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities
- Certified Safety Professional preferred

title: Sr. Regional Environmental Engineer, AWS Environmental Team
descriptionHtml:
Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental professionals who play a leading role in environmental permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. The work of our Regional Environmental Engineers is critical to enabling AWS's growth in the US and around the world.

The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth around the world, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

You will partner with AWS stakeholders to develop regional and site-specific development strategies enabling the construction and operation of AWS datacenters and infrastructure. You will lead environmental due diligence for site selection and acquisition, develop and execute regional and site-specific environmental permitting strategies, support environmental compliance during design and construction, and prepare for data center operations. This role requires regular engagement throughout the development lifecycle with multiple AWS stakeholders including Real Estate, Legal, Risk, Water, Design, Public Policy, Construction, and Operational teams, as well as external stakeholders including regulatory agencies, consultants, and contractors.

A successful candidate in this role will have a proven track record of delivering multiple, high-priority projects with tight timelines that require strong communication with partner teams, outside consultants and counsel, and regulatory agencies. The candidate must have a strong understanding of multi-media United States environmental permitting, remediation, and compliance requirements associated with large-scale infrastructure including experience with Clean Water Act (CWA) 404 and NPDES permitting. Preference in experience with OH EPA, IDEM, MO EDQ.


Key job responsibilities
- Assess environmental risks and requirements and develop mitigations and strategies to support data center siting and development strategies and site-specific project delivery.
- Lead technical aspects of environmental due diligence, including Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, regulatory and permitting evaluations, natural, biological and cultural resource evaluations, and noise assessments.
- Deliver environmental permits, approvals, and plans to enable on-time and compliant construction and operations for new data center locations and expansion of existing sites.
- Communicate environmental requirements, risks, and activities to internal and external project partners.
- Coordinate with partner teams including Real Estate, Design, Water, Legal, Risk, Power, and others to optimize site designs to consider natural resource or operational constraints.
- Develop site development and permitting strategies that are environmentally responsible and sustainable while meeting project timelines.
- Lead regulatory agency interactions and negotiations in support of environmental permit acquisition and regional development strategies.
- Develop, manage and track metrics to evaluate project success

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

In this role, you will partner with business leaders to deliver HR initiatives focused on talent management, employee engagement, and internal customer service. Success requires leveraging data-driven insights and understanding the importance of HR metrics to drive business impact. You may also lead a team of entry-level HR employees and own projects that enhance the employee experience.

The HR Business Partner balances strategic and tactical responsibilities, driving organizational success through partnership with leaders. They execute core PXT processes while providing guidance on talent processes, performance management, and cultural initiatives. By building trust and influence through sound business acumen, they manage increasingly complex issues and deliver solutions that enhance both employee experience and business outcomes.

descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, Finance has the unique challenge of stewarding and bolstering tremendous business growth through applying financial acumen, objectivity and leadership, while staying nimble and adaptive to evolving business needs. title: Data Center Engineering Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
How would you like to be a part of Earth’s most customer-centric company? You would work with teams of front-line responders who support the operations of some of the world’s most powerful data centers. Our Data Center Engineering Operations team maintain and operate our critical infrastructure systems so that they are prepared to stand up against any situation.

AWS has the world’s largest cloud computing portfolio. As an Amazonian you will work in some of the most sophisticated, safe, and secure data centers in the world. Our Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT’s) help keep them that way by working with the brightest minds from around the globe to help test and implement the newest technology and work practices to meet the demands of a changing market.

We have a passion for learning and evolving, it’s how we have helped define ourselves as leaders in the industry. Let’s work hard, have fun, and make history!

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Work Schedule:
Our Data Centers operate 24/7 and require on-site presence. This position offers two shift schedule options:

Option 1: Weekend Rotation
- Days Worked: Sunday - Tuesday, plus every other Saturday
- Weekly Pattern: Alternates between 3-day and 4-day work weeks
- Shift Hours: 5:30am - 6:00pm (day shift) OR 5:30pm - 6:00am (night shift)

Option 2: Weekday Rotation
- Days Worked: Wednesday - Friday, plus every other Saturday
- Weekly Pattern: Alternates between 3-day and 4-day work weeks
- Shift Hours: 5:30am - 6:00pm (day shift) OR 5:30pm - 6:00am (night shift)

Both schedules follow a rotating pattern where you'll work 3 days one week and 4 days the following week.

Overtime & Pay
- Overtime: Time and a half after 40 hours per week
- Night Shift Differential: 13% additional pay (6:00pm - 6:00am shifts)
- Maximum Hours: 60 hours per week in total (up to 20 hours of overtime)

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic qualifications

- Work shifts longer than eight hours in duration
- 2+ years of practical experience in electrical systems, mechanical systems, HVAC, and/or fire suppression systems
- Can bend or twist the body into unusual positions while working, use hands to manipulate small wires and objects, walk on job sites in uneven terrain, and work at heights and from ladders

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in data center engineering

• Build positive relationships with state and local policymakers.
• Build and manage relationships with trade associations, think tanks, and policymaker organizations.

You will monitor and analyze state and local public policy developments across Massachusetts and the Northeast, connecting legislative and regulatory activity to Amazon's business priorities. You will develop policy positions and strategies, engage directly with policymakers and their staff, and represent Amazon at policymaker conferences and industry events. title: Senior Engineer, CNC
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an exceptional Senior Engineer of CNC to own the machine tools that will produce the highest cost content in our product.

Precision machining is the established process for our actuator components and gears, and the equipment you select sets cycle time, machine count and cost per part at volume. Multi axis machining centers, turning, grinding, gear cutting and finishing, EDM and metrology, along with the automation and work holding around them. You will commit long lead equipment ahead of production need and work directly with process engineering on capability requirements at tolerances and hardness levels that leave very little margin.

This is a builder role in a zero to one manufacturing environment. There is no incumbent equipment base and no established supplier list. You will build both, and what you specify will still be running when we are producing at a rate no program has reached.

Key job responsibilities
- Machining Equipment Sourcing: Own end-to-end capital equipment sourcing, including supplier identification, market analysis, RFQ/RFP execution, total cost of ownership modeling, and award decisions across multi-axis CNC machining centers, turning centers, grinding, gear cutting and finishing, EDM, deburring and cleaning, metrology, and the automation and work-holding supporting them. Develop and implement sourcing approaches that optimize cost efficiency while advancing technical capabilities. Build machine-rate and cycle-time models that translate equipment selection into cost per part at volume.
- Contract Negotiations: Lead complex negotiations with OEMs, equipment manufacturers, integrators and service providers, structuring commercial agreements covering pricing, payment terms, warranties, acceptance criteria, run-at-rate and capability protocols, SLAs, and long-lead-time components, and managing the full contract lifecycle including amendments, renewals, and dispute resolution.
- Long-Lead Commitment and Schedule Risk: Own the machining equipment commitment calendar against factory move-in and start-of-production dates. Flag items where lead time exceeds available schedule and drive mitigation through slot reservations, phased releases or alternate suppliers.
- Process and Tooling Partnership: Work with Manufacturing and Process Engineering on machine capability requirements, including tolerance, concentricity, surface finish and hardness. Support cutting tool, fixture and work-holding strategy as part of total cost.
- Procurement Frameworks: Develop sourcing frameworks, standard operating procedures, and operating mechanisms that scale with the organization, supporting and mentoring sourcing managers and buyers through technical guidance.
- Supplier Performance Management: Establish and manage supplier performance programs, including scorecards, SLAs, and regular business reviews. Identify and mitigate supply chain risks through dual-sourcing strategies, should-cost models, and contingency planning. Assess supplier capability to build, install and commission at rate, not only to quote.
- Budget Management: Manage capital budgets with cost controls, variance tracking, and change management governance. Support material planning, inventory strategy, and spare parts availability. Drive cost optimization initiatives with demonstrated results.
- Cross-Functional Partnership: Align equipment procurement timelines with site milestones and schedules in close partnership with cross-functional teams across the organization. Serve as a procurement subject matter expert in cross-functional planning forums. Influence leadership on strategic direction and investment decisions related to the supply chain.

About the team
Amazon is building the next generation of robotics technology, and this role is key to our vision. Our Supply Chain team is responsible for standing up and scaling the procurement, sourcing, and supplier management functions. We are a small, high-impact team solving complex problems at the intersection of technology and production, and we are looking for builders who want to shape something from the ground up.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Finance, or a related technical field
- 6+ years of experience in supply chain management, strategic sourcing, or procurement in manufacturing, industrial automation, or similar technical environment
- Experience managing capital equipment procurement programs and vendor portfolios for complex environments, including equipment, automation, and tooling
- Experience leading contract negotiations with OEMs, equipment manufacturers, or construction contractors for agreements of significant value
- Experience developing sourcing strategies, procurement frameworks, or standard operating procedures
- Experience sourcing machine tools, precision metalworking equipment or related production automation

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in automotive, aerospace, medical device, automation, semiconductors, high-tech, or similar industries
- Direct sourcing experience with machine tool OEMs
- Working knowledge of machining processes and capability, including multi-axis milling, turning, grinding, gear hobbing and grinding, hard turning, and EDM
- Familiarity with machine capability and acceptance testing, including FAT, SAT, Cmk and Cpk studies, ballbar and laser calibration, and run-at-rate
- Understanding of cycle time, machine utilization and cost-per-part modeling, and how equipment selection drives machine count at volume
- Experience with cutting tool, fixture and work-holding sourcing as part of total cost of ownership
- Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems (SAP, Oracle, or similar)
- Six Sigma, Lean, or other continuous improvement certifications
- Experience managing significant capital budgets with demonstrated cost optimization results

title: Construction Estimator, AMER Estimating and Cost Control
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. Our Data Center Planning and Delivery (DCPD) organization builds and scales the infrastructure that powers AWS. We are seeking a Construction Estimator specializing in mechanical scope to join the newly formed AMER Estimating and Cost Control (ECC) organization as a discipline subject matter expert.

This is a technical individual contributor role. You will provide blue-badge, bottoms-up mechanical estimating capability for AWS data center construction across AMER and even globally in collaboration with EMEA and APJC Regional Estimating functions. Your focus spans the full mechanical scope of a data center — chilled water and cooling systems, CRAHs/CRACs and air handling, pumps and piping, chillers and cooling towers, refrigerant and liquid-cooling systems, plumbing, and the mechanical content of controls and commissioning packages.

You will collaborate globally with estimating teams across all AWS regions on BOD cost inputs that inform design standards. When Design Engineering introduces a mechanical design change or innovation, you are the first call — delivering rapid, discipline-specific cost impact assessments that enable informed decisions. This role is foundational to ECC’s mission of creating a structured feedback loop between estimate and actual, so estimates improve every cycle.


Key job responsibilities
- Produce detailed, bottoms-up mechanical construction cost estimates — chilled water and cooling systems, CRAHs/CRACs, air handling, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, piping, liquid-cooling, and plumbing
- Collaborate globally with regional estimating teams on Basis of Design (BOD) mechanical cost inputs that - Deliver rapid cost impact assessments for mechanical PDCM intercepts, first-of-kind designs, and innovation proposals from Design Engineering
- Support new regions planning with mechanical estimates for market entry — pre-Cost Breakdown Structure cost intelligence where local pricing data is thin
- Perform detailed mechanical quantity takeoff and pricing from flow diagrams, equipment schedules, specifications, and design documents at all design stages
- Develop and maintain the mechanical cost database — unit rates, $/ton and $/MW parametric models, and equipment pricing reflecting current market conditions and AWS standards
- Serve as the mechanical estimating SME for Estimating Managers, reviewing and validating 3P vendor mechanical estimates
- Analyze mechanical subcontractor pricing, bid tabulations, and awarded contracts to identify trends, anomalies, and cost optimization opportunities
- Benchmark mechanical estimates against portfolio actuals through the estimate-to-actual feedback loop with Cost Control
- Contribute to estimating tools and templates, incorporating lessons learned from completed projects into improved mechanical estimating methodologies


A day in the life
Your morning begins with a quantity takeoff on a Design intercept from Design Engineering — a proposed cooling system change (e.g., a shift in liquid-cooling approach) that could reduce installed cost but adds complexity. You model the delta against the current BOD mechanical estimate and prepare a cost impact memo for DE’s design review.

Midday, you join a global call with mechanical estimating counterparts in EMEA and APJC to align on BOD mechanical cost inputs — chilled-water $/ton, CRAH pricing, and piping unit rates — for the next design standard revision. Your AMER actuals are the benchmark. Afterward, an Estimating Manager asks you to gut-check a 3P vendor’s mechanical estimate; you spot a piping and pump-sizing assumption that doesn’t match the latest flow diagrams and flag it.

You close the day updating your mechanical cost database with final account data — a chiller package landed 6% above estimate in a competitive-bid market. You document the driver and adjust unit rates for the next round of estimates.


About the team
AMER Estimating and Cost Control (ECC) is a newly formed organization within DCPD that unifies Estimating and Cost Control under a single leader. ECC provides end-to-end cost lifecycle ownership — from initial estimate through final account.

You will be one of several Discipline Estimators (Electrical, Mechanical, CSA) working alongside the Estimating Managers who cover cluster groups across AMER, all reporting to the Manager, Construction Estimating (Chief Estimator Equivalent). Estimating provides the inputs — methodology, rates, benchmarks, discipline takeoffs, and 3P vendor products — that support Preconstruction’s owned estimates and CAR deliverables. Your electrical expertise directly supports both project-level estimating and global design standard development.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- Experience interpreting and modifying mechanical and electrical drawings
- 5+ years of experience in mechanical/HVAC construction cost estimating for commercial, industrial, or infrastructure projects
- Demonstrated experience with detailed mechanical quantity takeoff and pricing from flow diagrams, equipment schedules, and specifications
- Strong knowledge of chilled-water and cooling systems, air handling, chillers, pumps, piping, and mechanical installation practices
- Proficiency with estimating tools (e.g., Trimble/QuickPen, FastPIPE/FastDUCT, Bluebeam, On-Screen Takeoff, RSMeans, or equivalent)

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure experience
- Knowledge of critical data center equipment
- Experience in project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure
- Experience working in international cross-functional teams
- Experience with mechanical BOD estimating and $/MW parametric modeling

title: Principal Technical Product Manager, Quick Sight - Structured Data Analytics
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Quick is a decision intelligence service for the AI era. Today, thousands of enterprises and millions of users rely on Quick to connect their data, generate insights, and turn decisions into action — whether through interactive dashboards, embedded analytics woven into the products their customers use, natural language experiences that let any knowledge worker ask a question and get an answer they can act on immediately or fully managed tools that they can build and deploy for their stakeholders. 1000s of ISVs and SaaS companies have already built Quick into the fabric of their applications, powering experiences for millions of end users who benefit from intelligent, data-driven products. That is the kind of reach we operate at — and we are just getting started.

We are now at an inflection point. The convergence of structured data analytics, natural language interfaces, and agentic AI is rewriting the rules of what a decision intelligence service can do — not just for analysts, but for every knowledge worker in an enterprise. Quick sits at the center of this shift. We're building the service that lets an enterprise analyst build a governed dashboard in minutes, an ISV embed AI-powered analytics into their product with a few API calls, and a business leader ask a question in plain English and receive an insight they can turn into action before the day is over. The same service. The same governed data. One experience that scales from a single user to an entire organization — unlocking productivity, surfacing new opportunities, and accelerating businesses that are powered by data.

We are hiring a product leader for structured data analytics product team to own critical parts of this journey. This role spans some of the most consequential product areas in cloud analytics and decision intelligence today:

The data and intelligence foundation — how enterprises bring structured and unstructured data together under a unified semantic and governance layer that powers both BI reporting and AI-driven insights that turn into action.
Embedding and ISV enablement — how thousands of companies build differentiated, analytics-rich products on top of Quick's capabilities, and how we make that experience so seamless it becomes the default choice for every builder.
Business model and growth strategy — how we design packaging, pricing, and adoption pathways that make it effortless for customers to start, experiment, and scale with us — turning first deployments into enterprise-wide commitments.

What unites these roles is a shared profile: a deeply technical product leader who is equal parts strategist and practitioner. Someone who can see the three-year arc of a market and then roll up their sleeves to ship the next release. Someone who works backward from the customer's deployment — not from a requirements document — and who measures their own success by whether the customer succeeded. Someone who sees a nascent, fast-growing business not as a risk but as a canvas.

Quick is a business that is growing, evolving, and actively being shaped by the people on this team. You will have a direct and visible thumbprint on a service that is becoming the decision intelligence layer for enterprises and AI-powered products alike. The decisions you make — about what we build, how we package it, who we build it for, and how we bring it to market — will define how thousands of organizations and millions of knowledge workers experience data, make decisions, and take action in the age of AI.

If you are a builder who gets energy from ambiguity, who thinks in systems but ships in increments, and who wants to be at the frontier of where decision intelligence meets artificial intelligence — we want to talk to you.

Key job responsibilities
- Drive product delivery in deep partnership with engineering, applied science, and design. Drive product specifications, make crisp tradeoff decisions, and ensure high bar on the quality and user experience
- Be hands-on with the technology. Whether that means understanding how a semantic model resolves a natural language query, how an embedded analytics SDK integrates into a partner's React app, or how a pricing SKU flows through AWS billing — you operate at the level of detail where real product decisions are made.
- Own broad customer journeys from first contact through enterprise-wide adoption for critical engagement. Partner with GTM and Sales teams to design onboarding pathways, migration playbooks, and growth motions that reduce friction, accelerate time-to-value, and turn successful deployments into organization-wide productivity gains.
- Engage directly with enterprise customers, ISV partners, and AWS field teams. Turn what you hear into product conviction — not just feature requests, but insight into where the market is moving and what customers will need before they know to ask for it.
- Directly contribute to business outcomes — adoption, revenue, competitive win rates, customer retention. Use data relentlessly to prioritize, to make the case for investment, and to communicate progress to senior leadership.

A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing customer adoption metrics and operational dashboards, then shift into a working session with engineering and design partners to refine an upcoming feature launch. After lunch, you could be authoring a technical white paper or preparing a strategic narrative for leadership review. Later, you may lead a session with C-suite Data and AI executives on how their enterprise data can be turned into business outcomes using AWS analytics. Throughout it all, you bring clarity to tough trade-offs and ensure every stakeholder has the context they need.

About the team
Our team is focused on building and evolving externally facing services that empower businesses of all sizes to succeed. We operate with a strong sense of ownership and collaborate closely with science, research, engineering, design, marketing, and sales partners to deliver AI powered products that customers love and see how they can accelerate business value. We value decisiveness, curiosity, creative problem-solving, and a commitment to raising the bar for one another while being deeply technical and obsess about working backwards from customer problems.

Basic qualifications

- Experience delivering large-scale SaaS, PaaS or LaaS products where you are responsible for the full product lifecycle, from concept through GTM (go to market)
- 7+ years of working as a Technical Product Manager experience
- 5+ years of technical (software development, network development, IT, other related) experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience leading engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning

title: Software Development Engineer II, Amazon FinAuto - Travel & Events
descriptionHtml:
The Amazon Travel & Events (AT&E) Tech team, part of Finance Automation, is driving a multi-year transformation of the end-to-end Travel & Expense experience for over 500,000 Amazon employees across 64 countries. We are consolidating previously fragmented travel, events, payments, and expense systems into a unified, AI-powered experience within AtoZ, organized around four interconnected modules: Plan, Book, Pay, and Expense. Our platform leverages machine learning, natural language processing, and GenAI to deliver context-aware policy guidance, proactive compliance recommendations, fraud detection, and sustainability intelligence embedded into employee workflows. The transformation eliminates significant administrative burden across the organization while delivering substantial cost savings and recovering employee productivity at scale.

We are seeking a passionate Software Development Engineer who can help us build the next generation of unified Travel & Expense systems and support the AT&E organization.

As a Software Development Engineer on the team, you will design and build services that power AI-driven policy guidance, intelligent booking experiences, automated expense workflows, centralized payment mechanisms, and real-time T&E analytics serving a global customer base. You will collaborate with product managers, data scientists, and senior and peer-level software engineers across Finance Automation and partner organizations including Accounts Payable and Global Corporate Procurement. This role provides you with autonomy and ownership over decisions, working backwards directly from customers. There is ample opportunity for growth due to the high-visibility work and presence of senior engineering talent for guidance and mentorship. The team operates in cross-functional two-pizza team structures that lead T&E technical transformations.

You will contribute to a three-tier AI architecture that answers employee policy questions in under 2 seconds with source references, and proactively surfaces policy-compliant recommendations during booking to prevent violations before they occur. You will build modern, mobile-first travel booking and Meetings & Events hub experiences across 45+ countries with real-time validation and calendar integration. You will develop guided workflows, automated data integration pipelines, and conversational agents that significantly reduce expense report submission time and eliminate a meaningful share of expense reports entirely. You will build virtual payment capabilities and central card automation that reduce out-of-pocket employee spend and target zero manual reconciliation. You will develop AI/ML-powered fraud detection models that automate the majority of investigation checks and support transaction-based detection across expanding payment avenues. You will build a single-source T&E analytics platform providing real-time spend insights, policy violation tracking, and cost optimization visibility for managers and finance partners.


Key job responsibilities
- Design and implement scalable service architectures that power AI-driven policy guidance, intelligent booking, and automated expense workflows for a global user base.
- Deliver working features across the full software development lifecycle, from requirements and design through implementation, testing, deployment, and operations.
- Collaborate with product managers, applied scientists, and engineers across Finance Automation and partner organizations to translate business needs into reliable technical solutions.
- Coach teammates through code reviews and design discussions, raising the quality bar for the team's software and establishing shared engineering best practices.
- Identify and resolve root causes of operational issues while continuously improving system reliability and maintainability.

About the team
The Amazon Travel and Events Tech team sits within Finance Automation and is on a multi-year mission to unify how Amazon employees plan, book, pay for, and expense business travel and events worldwide. We are a collaborative, inclusive group of engineers, product managers, and scientists who value clear thinking and pragmatic design. If you want to build products at global scale that make a tangible difference in how people work, we would love to hear from you.

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience

In each fulfillment center, our teams stow deliveries, pick products, package them up and ship them out; each of these groups have played their part in taking us where we are today. The team drives process control and shifting mean performance with the outcome of minimizing variation between shifts, building and region, to deliver strong performance. The team works closely with Process System Engineering (PSE), ACES PM, Central Ops, launch teams, operations engineering and reliability and maintenance (RME) teams to improve the input metrics for each of the process paths by prioritizing and channelling resources.

The Site Process Engineer works alongside with the FC Senior Leadership Team, while keeping high collaboration with EU PE functions. This role is responsible to deploy initiatives, build networking and relationship in the FC and drive compliance for the initiatives within an assigned timeline. The Site Process Engineer initiates and implements EU wide improvement activities. This role requires the ability to demonstrate ownership for initiatives, understand the initiatives in details, and influence to deliver meaningful results translating to tangible productivity and efficiency gains in the FC.

Key job responsibilities
• Work on Back to Basics (B2B) initiatives identifying the top opportunities in the FC in comparison with the other EU FCs. Start from the bottom 50% processes, looking for the input metrics with the biggest gap to Benchmark and implement the improvement action plan in close collaboration with the local Operations Management team following the standard improvement templates.
a. Oversee the FC improvement program and set focus on most important areas, based on the alignment with the FC Senior Leadership team.
b. Dive deep into the process performance by using available standard reporting or create own data analysis, call out in in the daily dive deep meetings and collect feedback from the local team to be able to convert this information into a tangible improvement plan, that matters to the FC.
c. Review the open Action Plans on weekly basis, engaging the FC stakeholders to complete the suggested actions and reach the desired targets.
d. Collaborate with the central PE functions and other Site PEs from the same region to clarify any doubt process related and leveraging on their level of expertise. Benchmarking initiatives are highly recommended to further reduce variation across the FCs.
• Work on Continuous Improvement with the FC
a. Drive network best practice implementation, leveraging local initiative led with local Ops and share them to EU PE for the review. Once approved the best practice will be officially added to all EU Best Practice repository. This process is fundamental to help the top 50% FCs to reach Best In Class through the Variation Reduction process.
b. Strengthen the framework used to capture and scale FC innovation. New ideas and projects from the FC will flow through a standard process and presented to ACES process SMEs for the review.
c. Ensure big projects / ideas from the FC (10M$+ WW saving) are captured in the Operating Plan Q1 (OP1) Project Intake every year.
• Own the deployment of all the EU network initiatives assigned to the FC, making sure that they are executed with the right timeline, reaching compliance. Support the FC to commit on test and pilot for the EU Projects in order to avoid delays and make sure that projects are then deployed and reviewed in all the EU FCs.

• Partnership with the FC Ops:
a. Join the daily Gemba on the floor with FC Leadership in order to stay aligned with FC top issues and Associate feedback.
b. Organize the weekly LSC Meeting with the FC Leadership Team updating the Team on EU Variation Reduction, EU Projects rolled out in the FC, FC Best practices shared at EU level and FC local initiatives eligible for test or pilot.
c. Support the Site Leader and the FC Senior Management Team creating a strong relationship with them, which allows the Site PE to gain their trust and buy-in for all the initiatives. Beside standard task, SPE can support Site Leader and Senior Ops on process related ad hoc tasks from the FC accounting for less than 10% of the working time.
• Be ready to support or lead EU Projects to expand the initial scope and coordinate more than one FC. This opportunity is really important to improve project management skills and to deal with external stakeholders.
• During Q4 you will be deployed to the site management operational team, based on the need of the building.
• Ability to travel as needed within your area of responsibility. Domestic and regional travel estimate average: 0-10%. (Subject to change based on business need).

descriptionHtml:

In this role, you will partner with business leaders to deliver HR initiatives focused on talent management, employee engagement, and internal customer service. Success requires leveraging data-driven insights and understanding the importance of HR metrics to drive business impact. You may also lead a team of entry-level HR employees and own projects that enhance the employee experience.

The HR Business Partner balances strategic and tactical responsibilities, driving organizational success through partnership with leaders. They execute core PXT processes while providing guidance on talent processes, performance management, and cultural initiatives. By building trust and influence through sound business acumen, they manage increasingly complex issues and deliver solutions that enhance both employee experience and business outcomes.

You will be expected to work onsite at an Amazon facility.

Establish and implement mechanisms that ensure consistent, fair application of policies while maintaining compliance with evolving regulations.

From coaching leadership teams on workforce and talent management to driving HR process excellence, you'll collaborate with business leaders to develop forward-looking strategies focused on operational objectives and team effectiveness. You'll build strong partnerships across all levels of the organization while contributing to meaningful workplace improvements.

Success in this role comes from your ability to navigate organizational dynamics, lead change initiatives, and make high-judgment decisions in ambiguous situations. Through a combination of business acumen, data-driven insights, and strategic partnerships, you'll help create a workplace culture where employees feel valued and empowered, while driving long-term organizational success and adaptability in a rapidly evolving business landscape.

title: (Physical) Security Specialist Intern -  2027 Internship
descriptionHtml:
NO CYBERSECURITY, READ DESCRIPTION

Amazon's data centers house the infrastructure that powers the world's largest cloud. Protecting them is mission-critical — and as a Security Specialist Intern at Amazon Web Services (AWS), you will help ensure the physical security of these facilities from the inside.

You will drive operational security excellence, write reports, create presentations, and communicate with management on the status of physical security operations. Are you ready to embrace the challenge? Come build the future with us.

This internship is designed as a potential pathway to full-time employment. Interns who demonstrate strong performance throughout their internship may be considered for a full-time Security Specialist position, subject to available roles and business needs.

Who Should Apply

We welcome applications from:

- Students in the last year of their Technical/Bachelor's degree in Risk Management, Security Management, Criminology, or a related field who are looking for an internship that could lead to a full-time career.

About the Role

As a Security Specialist Intern, you will work within the Data Center Security team and play a hands-on role in the day-to-day physical security operations of Amazon's data centers. You will collaborate with security vendors, analyze operational data, and help identify improvements to surveillance systems, access controls, and security procedures.

This is not a desk-only role. You will engage directly with the people, systems, and processes that keep Amazon's most critical infrastructure safe.

What You Will Do
- Coordinate with vendors involved in new security construction, repairs, daily security operations and patrols, and planning.
- Analyze security metrics and data to identify trends and recommend improvements
- Make suggestions on improving electronic surveillance systems and access controls
- Help develop and deliver guidance to data center occupants on reducing false alarms
- Write reports and create presentations on the status of physical security operations for management
- Assist with planning and coordinating security-related projects
- Support incident documentation and follow-up processes

Internship Structure

Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for 12 consecutive weeks. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Monday through Friday.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed below, we encourage you to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let that stop you from applying.

Your Career at Amazon — A Universe of Opportunity

At Amazon, your career is not a straight path. It is a journey you build as you go.

From your first day as an intern, you will own real work that matters. You will help protect the infrastructure that keeps AWS running for millions of customers. Your mentors and teammates will champion your growth, helping you build skills you did not know existed — and you will see your work come to life at massive scale.

Impact. Your work protects the physical infrastructure that millions of customers rely on every day. The security operations you support keep Amazon's most critical facilities safe and running.

Action. You will move fast, analyze real security data, and make recommendations that get implemented. Your ideas do not stay theoretical — they get tested and put into practice.

Curiosity. Every project teaches you something new. You will learn how physical security operates at world-class scale and explore different teams, technologies, and career paths within Amazon.

Mentorship and career growth. You will start with structured onboarding and get paired with experienced mentors. Our team is dedicated to supporting new members in an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing. Projects and tasks are assigned in a way that leverages your strengths and helps you further develop your skill set. Your journey here is yours to shape.


About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on.

You will join a diverse team of engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers.

Basic qualifications

- In pursuit of a Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Risk Management, Security Management, Criminology or a related field, graduating in 2027
- Ability to work well with others in a team environment, with strong time management skills
- Own vehicle is recommended as reliable transportation to the data center facility (note: public transit option is not available)

Preferred qualifications

- Strong communication skills
- Ability to learn and adapt quickly to company tools for data gathering and analysis
- Metrics oriented
- Ability to act swiftly and calmly in time of crisis
- Ability to handle confidential information with care
- Ability to integrate into an international work environment

Amazon est un employeur engagé pour l'égalité des chances. Nous sommes convaincus qu'une main d'oeuvre diversifée est essentielle à notre réussite. Nous prenons nos décisions de recrutement en fonction de votre expérience et de vos compétences. Nous apprécions votre envie de découvrir, d'inventer, de simplifier et de construire. La protection de votre vie privée et la sécurité de vos données constituent depuis longtemps une priorité absolue pour Amazon. title: Program Manager III, Strategic Initiatives Team
descriptionHtml:
The NAMER Cloud Sales Center (CSC) is AGS's primary scale revenue engine and its most important talent developer, delivering $4B in revenue and ambitious annual growth. Early career talent sits at the heart of that engine: these sellers feed up to 60% of Field sellers and contribute an outsized share of CSC pipeline. This role owns the front door to that system.

As Senior Program Manager for Early Career Talent & Employer Brand, you own how CSC attracts, selects, and launches the next generation of sellers, and how the market sees CSC as the place to start a career in cloud sales. You will own the internship program, the co-op program, and the broader early-career strategy that shapes the caliber, diversity, engagement, and readiness of everyone who enters AGS through this door. This is a role that is strategic and tactical in equal measure: you will set multi-year strategy while running live cohorts that deliver measurable, in-year business impact.

You will join a team of senior program leaders in the CSC Strategic Initiatives Team, each owning a connected part of the talent flywheel — enablement, talent strategy and matriculation, platforms and data, and partner activation. You own the top of that flywheel and the employer brand that fills it. Success looks like a high-caliber, diverse, engaged early-career pipeline that converts faster, ramps faster, and strengthens CSC's competitive position for the next generation of GenAI-native sellers.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the early-career talent portfolio end to end: Connect the internship program, co-op program, and strategy into a single entry-point to the CSC’s integrated talent engine
• Own CSC's early-career employer brand and talent profile: Define who we attract and how we are seen, while treating the caliber, diversity, and engagement of incoming talent as a strategic lever
• Set strategy and run execution: Design the multi-year early-career model while owning live cohorts and their in-year pipeline and conversion outcomes
• Feed the talent flywheel: Partner with leadership on matriculation timing and workforce-planning inputs so early-career talent flows predictably into onboarding, development, and Field roles
• Set and hold the intake quality bar: Ensure new talent is prepared for full-time roles, accelerating time to productivity and increasing impact
• Prove impact with data: Collaborate with data teams to instrument early-career conversion, ramp, and diversity metrics to clearly articulate ROI
• Amplify through partners: Connect employer-brand moments and early-career events into the broader partner activation strategy so they reinforce the wider engine
• Operate with executive visibility: Represent early-career talent as a named pillar of the org's talent strategy, with regular exposure to senior leadership and Field partners

A day in the life
You start the morning reviewing conversion and pipeline data from the current cohort with the data team, then join a working session with talent-strategy leadership on matriculation timing for the next intake. Before lunch you are refining the co-op model and the employer-brand plan for the next campus season. In the afternoon you sync with enablement on the intake quality bar, align an upcoming early-career event with the partner team, and close the day preparing a readout for senior leadership on the two things that matter most this quarter.

About the team
Our team is focused on delivering programs that have broad impact across Amazon. We work collaboratively with leaders across AWS to solve problems at scale. We value clear thinking, thoughtful communication, and a willingness to challenge assumptions in pursuit of the best outcomes. As we continue to grow, we are building an inclusive team culture where every voice matters and where program managers have the opportunity to shape strategy and drive results that customers feel directly.

About AWS
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

AWS Sales, Marketing, and Global Services (SMGS) is responsible for driving revenue, adoption, and growth from the largest and fastest growing small- and mid-market accounts to enterprise-level customers including public sector. The AWS Global Support team interacts with leading companies and believes that world-class support is critical to customer success. AWS Support also partners with a global list of customers that are building mission-critical applications on top of AWS services.

title: Principal Product Designer, AI/ML Services
descriptionHtml:
AWS AI Services is seeking a Principal UX Designer to lead some of the most strategic and complex design initiatives across our AI/ML portfolio, including Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

This is an individual contributor role for a designer who operates beyond the boundaries of a single product or feature area. You will tackle large-scale, highly ambiguous customer problems that span services, workflows, and organizations, establish experience vision and strategy where the path forward is not yet defined, and influence product direction across AWS AI Services.

This is a particularly exciting moment to work in this space. Generative AI and agents are changing not only what developers can build, but how software itself is built, evaluated, deployed, and operated. Many of the interaction models for these technologies are still emerging. You will have the opportunity to work on capabilities at the frontier of AI development and help define patterns that do not yet have established answers.

You will work at the intersection of AI platform strategy, developer experience, and emerging interaction models, translating sophisticated technical capabilities into experiences that help builders move from experimentation to production. You’ll partner with senior leaders across Product, Engineering, Applied Science, Research, and UX to identify systemic customer problems, create alignment around a future-state vision, and turn that vision into shipped experiences.

This is hands-on design role. You’ll move fluidly between strategy and execution, framing problems, conducting and using customer research, mapping complex systems and workflows, prototyping new interaction models, defining end-to-end experiences, and working directly with engineering teams to ship them.

Key job responsibilities
Lead strategic, portfolio-level design initiatives. Take on some of the most consequential and ambiguous customer problems across Bedrock, AgentCore, and the broader AWS AI/ML portfolio. Many of these challenges will cross product and organizational boundaries, requiring you to see the larger system, define a clear experience vision, and bring multiple teams together around a path forward.

Define the future of AI developer experiences. Help shape how builders create, evaluate, deploy, govern, and operate generative AI applications and agents on AWS. In a space where many interaction patterns are still being invented, you’ll have the opportunity to establish new models for how developers work with AI and influence experiences that span the console, APIs, SDKs, and CLI.

Shape the technology, not just the interface. Great developer experiences often begin well below the UI. You’ll go deep into the architecture, APIs, data models, and developer workflows behind the products you design, working directly with senior engineers and technical leaders to make them more intuitive. That may mean influencing the structure of an API, challenging an abstraction that exposes too much underlying complexity, or rethinking terminology and defaults before they become difficult to change. You should be comfortable engaging Engineering at this level and advocating for a different technical solution when a technically valid one creates a poor customer experience.

Bring clarity to ambiguous problems. You’ll often begin with an emerging technology, an unmet customer need, or a broad strategic opportunity rather than a defined set of requirements. Use customer insight, systems thinking, prototyping, and strong product judgment to make the problem concrete, explore what is possible, and help teams converge on the right direction.

Set the quality bar through hands-on craft. This is a Principal role where you will continue to design and ship. Take on complex experiences yourself, explore alternatives and tradeoffs, prototype rapidly, validate ideas with customers, and carry the work from early concept through detailed execution. Move quickly while maintaining a high bar for interaction design, visual craft, and the details that make technical products easier to understand and use.

Create coherence across the portfolio. Look beyond individual products to identify where customers encounter fragmentation across AWS AI Services. Establish shared interaction models, frameworks, and patterns that solve those problems systematically and help Bedrock, AgentCore, and adjacent services feel like a connected builder experience.

Influence across organizational boundaries. Many of the problems you’ll own cannot be solved by one team. Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across Product, Engineering, Science, and UX, bring customer evidence and design thinking into strategic decisions, and create alignment when teams have different technical constraints, priorities, or points of view.

Raise the design bar beyond your own work. Your impact as a Principal designer should extend beyond the experiences you personally ship. Provide thoughtful critique and direction, develop approaches that other teams can reuse, mentor designers tackling complex technical problems, and help elevate the quality of design across the broader organization.

Basic qualifications

- 8+ years of design experience
- Have an available online portfolio
- Experience with best practices for User Interface Design, Information Architecture, and Interaction Design
- Experience in life cycle design projects from design strategy through execution
- Experience in a fast-paced, high-tech company, or experience completing complex tasks quickly with little to no guidance and react with appropriate urgency to situations that require a quick turnaround
- Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams including Marketing, Product Management, Customer Service, Operations, Legal, Finance, and Senior Leadership
- Experience providing training and mentorship
- 3+ years designing and shipping developer-facing AI/ML products. You understand the end-to-end agent development lifecycle, including model hosting, deployment, observability, evaluation. You design across APIs, SDKs, CLIs, and console experiences, with the technical depth to understand developer workflows and influence the underlying interfaces and abstractions.
- Ability to design in code-based prototypes and work comfortably with code

Preferred qualifications

- Experience providing and effectively communicating strategic and tactical recommendations based on data
- Experience designing and prototyping with tools such as Sketch, Photoshop, Illustrator, Axure, Keynote, and InVision
- Experience designing products for AWS or another major cloud platform, with an understanding of the needs of enterprise cloud customers.

title: Regional Asset Protection and Safety Manager, WWGS Retail Asset Protection Department
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS) is looking for a Regional Asset Protection and Safety Manager to lead the region in shrink reduction and profit maximization efforts. The position will proactively seek to bring economic value to the company, promoting profitable sales and world class customer service while ensuring a safe place to work and shop.

Key job responsibilities
- Monitors, manages and audits all aspects of physical security within assigned region to ensure alarm systems, access control and CCTV standards are operational and in compliance.
- Conducts detailed business audits to identify exposure to margin erosion, policy breakdowns, systemic issues and shrink opportunities.
- Analyzes work environment to control, eliminate and prevent accidents.
- Partners with Region Operations and Store Team Leaders.
- Acts as a subject matter expert, teacher and trainer for all matters pertaining to Asset Protection and Occupational Safety.
- Conducts financial and operational investigations relating to Safety program compliance, margin erosion, profit loss, and dishonesty. Utilizes data to identify opportunities and suggest business improvements.
- Partners with Team Member Services to complete investigations and interviews.
- Partners with the store teams to reduce accidents, cash and merchandise loss on the front end. Helps establish best practices and programs designed to minimize risk and improve service.
- Supports all Store Operations objectives to enhance service, safety and the profitability of the Region.
- Manages the Global Asset Protection / Safety Communications and Awareness program throughout the Region. Guides Store Team Leaders to achieve required Team Member participation rates, ensuring Team Members have the confidence and knowledge to successfully execute the Global Asset protection and Occupational Safety program.
- Maintains and understands statistical information, accident data and case reporting materials.
- Acts as a liaison between Federal, State and local law enforcement, third party security contractors, regulatory agencies, OSHA and Whole Foods Markets.
- Partners with the Regional Food Safety teams to ensure all regulatory and compliance expectations are being met to reduce incidents and maintain standards.
- Builds region specific shrink and accident reduction strategies and utilizes resources to achieve goals.
- Partners with region receiving team to ensure back room compliance measures are being executed.

This role is based out of a field site; however the majority of time (~70%) will be spent traveling to store locations within the assigned region rather than working from the base office. Overnight travel may be required depending on geographic scope of the assigned region.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent in business or a related field
- 5+ years of experience in multi-unit Retail Asset Protection and Safety.
- Wicklander-Zulawski trained

Preferred qualifications

- Loss Prevention Certified (LPC)
- Experience with OSHA regulations and workplace safety programs
- Certified Forensic Interviewer (CFI)
- Experience in grocery or specialty retail environments
- Proficiency with data analytics tools for loss prevention reporting
