title: Onsite Medical Representative
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. The Amazon Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) team sets the strategic direction to provide resources, best practices, and safe environments to proactively manage the health and wellbeing of our workforce. To support these goals, Amazon is seeking an experienced and dynamic Onsite Medical Representative (OMR) to join our team. In this position, you will work closely with the WHS Site Manager, WHS Specialist, and occasionally the Injury Prevention Specialist (IPS). This includes attending weekly associate safety committee meetings, greeting all new hires for the site or through daily one-on-one interaction. Additionally, the OMR will participate in weekly case management review meetings as necessary.

As an OMR, you will independently assess and administer first aid as well as offer guidance to Amazon Associates (AAs) on both occupational and non-occupational injuries or illnesses. You should be passionate about learning and advocating health and wellness principles to consistently support AAs on a daily basis. You will refer care to outside medical providers as needed, and learn about OSHA regulations, risk, and analysis.

The OMR will function as a part of the larger team onsite, assisting with all first aid needs and support safety operations as needed.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Provide first aid support and make referrals to outside medical providers as necessary.
- Minimize the AA risk of injury through awareness, education, and proactive engagement.
- Maintain all records of care provided to AAs.
- Coordinate and maintain the workers’ compensation and return to work programs for AAs with work-related injuries.
- Provide daily activity logs and end of shift reports.
- Engage with AAs and leadership on operations floor to provide coaching regarding observed at-risk work habits.
- Maintain a clean working environment and ensure appropriate medical supply inventory is maintained.
- Participate in training and certification to facilitate first aid, CPR and AED certifications classes.
- Maintain all first aid, CPR, AED credentials.
- Work flexible shifts which could include days, nights, holidays, and/or weekends.
- Assist with random saliva drug testing protocols.
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Current valid Basic Life Support (BLS) certification by an approved emergency cardiac care (ECC) provider; AND must have one of the following:
- Current valid Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) OR Paramedic Certification from the Department of Health OR the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians (NREMT); OR
- Current active Athletic Trainer Certification, by either the Board of Certification (BOC) or equivalent State Certification.

Preferred qualifications

- Certified to teach first aid, CPR, and AED training from American Heart Association or American Red Cross
- Proficient in Microsoft Office
- Experience with an industrial wellness program
- Experience managing musculoskeletal disorders, ergonomics, and coaching on body mechanics
- Demonstrated work experience with OSHA regulations and Workers Compensation
- Proficient in digital recordkeeping
- In the last year, six months job experience in the Military as a Combat Medic (U.S. Army), Field Medic (U.S. Army), Healthcare Specialist (U.S. Army), Hospital Corpsman (U.S. Navy), or Aerospace Medical Service Technician (U.S. Air Force)

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Los Angeles County applicants: Job duties for this position include: work safely and cooperatively with other employees, supervisors, and staff; adhere to standards of excellence despite stressful conditions; communicate effectively and respectfully with employees, supervisors, and staff to ensure exceptional customer service; and follow all federal, state, and local laws and Company policies. Criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship with some of the material job duties of this position. These include the duties and responsibilities listed above, as well as the abilities to adhere to company policies, exercise sound judgment, effectively manage stress and work safely and respectfully with others, exhibit trustworthiness and professionalism, and safeguard business operations and the Company’s reputation. title: Business Intelligence Engineer, Amazon Shipping
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s global fulfillment network enables any merchant to ship items that are ordered on Amazon to any place on earth. There is a complex network of ways in which items move between vendor locations, Amazon warehouses, and customer locations as well as several intermediate locations through which packages travel before reaching the customer. With a scale of millions of packages, each with different attributes and delivery requirements, what results is a highly dense graph of nodes.

We have built a highly respected BI and Data Engineering team which is focused on solving complex problems in worldwide transportation using workflows, optimization algorithms, and machine learning systems. These are large-scale distributed systems handling millions of packages being shipped through the Amazon logistics network.

As a Business Intelligence Engineer, you will develop datasets, dashboards, reports, and visualizations using BI tools, and provide data-driven recommendations to support strategic planning within Amazon Shipping. Additionally, you will deliver across planned projects that will improve overall cost and profitability for the business.


Key job responsibilities
- Data Management and Integration: Collect, process, and manage large datasets from various sources, ensuring data accuracy, consistency, and accessibility.

- Data Analysis: Analyze complex data sets to identify trends, patterns, and insights that can inform business decisions.

- Reporting and Visualization: Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, and visualizations to present data insights in an understandable and actionable format.

- Stakeholder Collaboration: Work closely with stakeholders to understand their data needs, provide data-driven recommendations, and support strategic planning.

- Tool and Technology Utilization: Utilize and stay updated with the latest BI tools and technologies to enhance data analysis and reporting capabilities.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of analyzing and interpreting data with Redshift, Oracle, NoSQL etc. experience
- Experience with data visualization using Tableau, Quicksight, or similar tools
- Experience with one or more industry analytics visualization tools (e.g. Excel, Tableau, QuickSight, MicroStrategy, PowerBI) and statistical methods (e.g. t-test, Chi-squared)
- Experience with scripting language (e.g., Python, Java, or R)

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree, or Advanced technical degree
- Knowledge of data modeling and data pipeline design
- Experience with statistical analysis, co-relation analysis

title: Software Dev Engineer II, Secure Customer Content Storage and Analytics, AWS Applied AI Solution – Core Services
descriptionHtml:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Join our Applied AI Solutions team and help build the secure data foundation that powers AWS's AI-driven business applications. We own critical infrastructure including event-based data stores, machine learning training platforms, and data access interfaces that enable responsible AI development while maintaining the highest standards of privacy, security, and compliance. Our platform serves as the backbone for storing, processing, and managing data that fuels AI-powered capabilities across AWS, ensuring customers retain full control over their information.

As a Software Development Engineer II, you'll take ownership of production systems that handle the complete data lifecycle—from ingestion through model training to customer opt-out controls. You'll maintain and refactor existing services for enhanced performance and scalability, while designing new solutions to meet emerging requirements from business application teams. Working alongside scientists and engineers, you'll enable them to build and improve AI models, balancing innovation with compliance requirements.

This role offers exciting opportunities to solve complex challenges around secure data storage, efficient querying at scale, and building self-service platforms that empower development teams. You'll drive the evolution of established platforms to meet future needs, directly impacting how AWS delivers increasingly sophisticated AI-powered capabilities while ensuring customers maintain complete control over their data throughout every stage of processing.


Key job responsibilities
- Own and deliver complete software features for event-based data storage systems, from design through deployment and operations, ensuring they provide flexible, secure, and compliant platforms for AI-powered business applications
- Maintain, refactor, and enhance existing storage and analytics platform, identifying opportunities to improve performance, scalability, and operational excellence while eliminating technical debt
- Design and implement software solutions for data access interfaces and authorization systems within established architectural strategies, seeking guidance from senior engineers when facing complex technical tradeoffs
- Mentor team members through code reviews, documentation, and knowledge sharing—providing meaningful feedback, training newcomers on system architecture, and facilitating technical discussions that promote operational excellence
- Resolve operational issues by identifying root causes and implementing permanent fixes for compliance features, data deletion APIs, and customer opt-out mechanisms, going beyond quick workarounds
- Work directly with business application teams and stakeholders to understand requirements, translating them into technical solutions that balance customer needs with platform sustainability
- Take ownership of security implementations including encryption, access controls, audit trails, and PII handling, ensuring software can be maintained and extended by other engineers
- Drive improvements to self-service platforms and control planes, making priority tradeoffs between new feature development and operational work while maintaining governance standards

A day in the life
You'll participate in engineering standups, providing updates on data storage features and resolving platform blockers. Your hands-on work includes refactoring services for performance, implementing secure data interfaces, and ensuring compliance through quality code and testing. You'll collaborate with scientists and engineers, helping them navigate data access patterns and authorization requirements while mentoring teammates through code reviews. When production issues arise, you investigate root causes to maintain reliable data deletion and opt-out mechanisms. Regular syncs with business application teams help you translate evolving requirements into technical solutions that balance innovation with security and compliance, while also documenting features and training teammates on system lifecycles.

About the team

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: DC Design Manager for Region (AMER), DCDE - AMER, Design Manager East team
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. title: Senior Software Development Engineer, Fauna
descriptionHtml:
Fauna Robotics is building capable, safe, and delightful robots for everyday life. We are hiring a Senior Software Development Engineer to build cloud services that keep the fleet humming. In this role, you will build the cloud foundation and applications that connect robots to customer experiences and internal operations as we scale.

The ideal candidate has built distributed systems that connect physical devices to cloud services end to end. They are comfortable building and operating the services they own from prototyping through launch and beyond. They make sound architectural tradeoffs across privacy, security, reliability, delivery speed, and cost when requirements are still evolving. They work effectively across robotics, product, and operations teams while remaining hands-on in design and implementation.

Key job responsibilities
- Build and own the cloud services that connect a growing fleet of robots to customer experiences and internal operations

- Build operational telemetry ingestion pipelines that process high-frequency robot signals

- Select technologies where the stack is undefined, document the decisions, and set patterns for a growing team

- Join the on-call rotation for the services you own and drive incident response

- Work with science, engineering, and product teams to define requirements and operationalize new workflows

About the team
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.

We believe that future won't arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We're changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.

Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We're building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.

At Fauna, you'll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It's an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.

If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we're interested in hearing from you.

- 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with device or fleet connectivity at scale: MQTT, device identity and certificate management, offline-tolerant sync, or an IoT platform (AWS IoT Core, Greengrass, or equivalent).
- Experience with real-time telemetry ingestion and streaming (Kafka, Kinesis, or time-series stores).
- Experience with over-the-air update delivery and staged fleet rollouts.
- Experience securing connected devices: secure provisioning, secrets management, and data privacy.
- Experience with infrastructure as code and operational tooling (Terraform, CDK, Kubernetes).
- Experience in robotics, automotive, connected home, or another domain where software runs on hardware in the field.

title: Senior Reliability Maintenance Engineering Technician, RME
descriptionHtml:
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team is central to Amazon's commitment to innovation. As Amazon evolves and adapts, this team makes sure that the tools and technologies we use do as well. As a Senior RME Technician, you'll help us stay one step ahead, adopting the latest technologies and identifying new and efficient ways of working. In this role, you’ll pay close attention to our processes to help maintain our high standards, and you’ll put in place upgrades to take that standard even higher.

Key job responsibilities
- Demonstrate best practice on using equipment safely and monitor teams to ensure everyone follows the correct processes
- Keep track of equipment performance through visual checks, condition-based monitoring, and preventative maintenance tasks and schedule additional servicing when required
- Supervise technicians on shift to support their development and act as the first point of contact for Reliability Maintenance Engineers
- Solve issues in equipment to reduce downtime for operations so they can process packages as quickly as possible
- Support in finding ways to continually improve systems and standardise processes across the EU network

A day in the life
Our RME Technicians are based on-site, so they can respond quickly to any machinery issues. You’ll carry out a range of planned preventative maintenance to our sites’ equipment to make sure it’s working safely. As an RME Technician, you’ll also respond promptly to breakdowns, investigating, finding, and implementing solutions as quickly as possible. You’ll also make suggestions for long-term improvements.

Working alongside senior colleagues, you’ll undertake day-to-day maintenance tasks and will liaise with contractors if you need external expertise. You’ll work on a range of shifts to make sure our sites are supported around the clock – allowing Amazon to deliver at the speed we’re known for.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or cutting-edge tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

Basic qualifications

- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year UK certified apprenticeship
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Experience in automated conveyors systems and controls, electrical and electronic principles, preventative maintenance procedures, blueprint and schematic reading, industrial electrical, industrial controls, industrial electronics, Programmable Logic Control (PLC) programs, National Electrical Code (NEC), work order management
- Experience leading teams

Preferred qualifications

-Associate's degree in Mechatronics or a related technical field
-Experience in vendor management
-Experience with robotic maintenance
-Experience leading engineering teams as a mentor or tech lead
-Experience working with material handling equipment (MHE) safety standards in accordance with OEM requirements

Your charter is not to report the number but to move it, finding where the largest quality gains are available, turning them into work for the teams who can deliver them, and making the call when a change that lifts one dimension costs another. You will partner closely with multiple engineering and science teams and will drive the cross-organizational decisions to define and influence the future of shopping AI.

About the team
Our mission is to fundamentally change how customers shop on Amazon by leveraging the state of the art in AI. Every month, hundreds of millions of customers use Alexa for Shopping to help with shopping decisions. We are building a conversational shopping experience that understands what customers need, provides trustworthy and helpful responses, and makes the entire shopping journey effortless. We will build the best shopping AI in the world — and then do it again in the next sprint.

descriptionHtml:

title: Senior Regional EHS Manager
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we prioritize health, safety, and well-being above all else. There is nothing more important. To support this priority, Amazon is seeking an experienced and innovative Senior Regional Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) Manager to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for partnering with a regional operations team to execute company WHS policies and ensure compliance to all applicable local, regional and federal regulations. By leveraging lean principles and kaizens, you will lead continuous improvement initiatives to reduce conditional and ergonomic risk to ensure a safe and healthful working environment for Amazon’s Associates.

In this role, you must demonstrate the ability to build trust and confidence with the cross functional operations teams, and influence change through providing comprehensive risk assessments and safety data analysis. To do so, you must be an effective communicator and send clear, concise and consistent messages, both verbally and in writing. You will also be required to instruct and train operations leadership and site WHS professionals in company EHS policies while assisting the regional teams in incorporating our safety standards at their sites. Your experience working in safety programs and your relevant safety, environmental and ergonomic knowledge in an operations environment will be crucial.

You will be responsible for developing a team of safety managers and safety professionals within your designated region. Your teams’ success will depend on your ability to create and execute leadership development plans for your larger team. You must demonstrate your ability to clearly communicate organizational direction through your team and give frequent and appropriate feedback to your WHS teams while ensuring they are executing to the core competencies of an Amazon WHS professional. As a senior leader in the WHS organization, you will also be responsible for judging and assessing safety talent to select appropriate bench strength for current and future business needs.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Act as SME of local/regional regulations and company WHS policy.
- Provide guidance and oversight to ensure compliance to all applicable Amazon WHS Policies.
- Measure the regions and sites’ performance against published requirements in WHS policies. For all deficiencies, identify a plan for the site to implement and fix all identified deficiencies.
- Ensure WHS recordkeeping and data integrity and provides Operations with accurate reporting and metrics to support business WHS initiatives.
- Deliver on-time and quality projects to Operations. Deliver quality projects on time to Operations.
- Analyze WHS metrics and review incident weekly and monthly incident trends to discover trends to justify the allocation of appropriate resources to areas where the safety risk is highest.
- Analyze Global Safety Peer Review results and develop and implement solutions to eliminate exposure to these risks and prevent injury at other FCs.
- Audit recordkeeping practices and Global WHS Database entries to ensure compliance to global WHS standards and local regulations.
- Audit the workplace organization and Associate behaviors to ensure that training, auditing and scoring methods are accurate and consistent.
- Manage and mentor the FC WHS Manager and WHS Associates in your assigned FCs.
- Spend time at the fulfillment centers and seek input from WHS teams, Associates and leaders on WHS program improvement opportunities. Ensure open communication on status of progress and resolution against these suggestions.
- Lead soft tissue injury reduction efforts by performing targeted Kaizens in partnership with the Operations teams based on the risks identified in each task (force, repetition, and awkward postures).
- Ensure site leadership and Associates are trained and knowledgeable of their responsibilities under each policy. Audit the quality, delivery (including qualifications of the trainer), and effectiveness of all required WHS training.
- Review for effectiveness the deployed WHS tools and revise to ensure continual improvement.
- Partner with corporate and other regional field WHS personnel to leverage global WHS and environmental best practices into NA network standards.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site

Those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

- 7+ years of increasing responsibilities in safety and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, service operations, or relevant experience applicable to the role
- 7+ years of increasing responsibilities in people and performance management
- Experience implementing lean principles and process improvement in an operational environment.
- Ability to travel up to 50%
- Office within one of the designated region's sites. Must be willing to relocate if not currently within region
- Willingness to work a variety of shifts, including nights and weekends, as required to support direct reports and site needs.

- Experience in a fast-paced, dynamic organization
- Interest in long-term career development through assignments in multiple business units across the nation
- Prior experience in a management development training program
- Track record of effectively managing a safety operation comprising both salaried and hourly staff
- Demonstrate experience in developing others into higher levels of responsibility in an organization

title: Sr. Regional Enviro Engineer -Water Compliance, AWS Environmental Team
descriptionHtml:
As a Regional Environmental Engineer (REE) specializing in water compliance, you will support water-related environmental compliance at AWS data centers. You will provide technical expertise in permitting and compliance across National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), Significant Industrial User (SIU) discharge, potable water systems, groundwater wells, onsite wastewater treatment systems, stormwater, and water-quality monitoring and reporting. You will evaluate existing and proposed infrastructure, develop scalable compliance programs and technical standards, monitor environmental performance, and partner with design, construction, operations, and other stakeholders to incorporate water-related regulatory requirements into site design and operation.

Key job responsibilities
• Lead water compliance programs for water supply and discharge across US data center locations
• Develop and maintain the water compliance program that guides how sites and REEs obtain, renew, modify, interpret, and implement NPDES and other water discharge permits under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and applicable state regulations, and translate effluent limitations, monitoring, operating, reporting, and notification requirements into site-level compliance programs
• Provide guidance on evaluating regulatory applicability and permitting requirements for new sites, expansions, operational changes, and new or modified discharges
• Provide guidance on evaluating industrial wastewater and stormwater permitting and compliance, including federal pretreatment under 40 CFR Part 403, local sewer-use ordinances, POTW requirements, pollution-prevention plans, inspections, best management practices, monitoring, and reporting
• Provide technical guidance on potable water systems and onsite wastewater systems, including design, operation, monitoring, and compliance under applicable drinking-water and septic requirements
• Develop standard templates and technical guidance for water-quality sampling and monitoring plans, review site plans, and set standards for sampling equipment, monitoring systems, and analytical methods under 40 CFR Part 136
• Evaluate water and wastewater treatment processes, system performance, waste-stream characterization, water balances, and discharge pathways to determine permitting and compliance implications
• Build the mechanisms, dashboards, and metrics that track water-quality data, lab reports, DMRs, and compliance performance, and support sites in identifying trends, exceedances, corrective actions, and forecasting across sites
• Read and evaluate engineering plans, process-flow diagrams, P&IDs, and specifications, and partner with design, engineering, construction, and operations teams to build water-related controls into current and future designs early
• Clearly communicate the technical and regulatory basis for environmental requirements and influence partner teams to implement compliant, practical, and scalable solutions
• Set the standards and oversight mechanisms that keep work by employees, contractors, and consultants aligned with applicable environmental requirements and Amazon standards
• Support REEs and sites in their interactions with regulatory agencies, utilities, POTWs, consultants, and contractors, and engage directly on program-level matters
• Support time-critical regulatory notifications, permit applications, and monitoring reports, and support emergency response planning and incident investigations, including root causes and corrective and preventive actions
• Develop and deliver water compliance training for relevant staff
• Stay current with evolving water regulations and industry best practices for domestic and non-contact cooling, particularly in the data center sector


About the team
The AWS Environmental is a team of professionals responsible for the environmental planning, delivery, and operational compliance of all AWS global infrastructure projects.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering
- 7+ years of eExperience with NPDES and industrial wastewater permitting and compliance, including interpreting effluent limitations, sampling/monitoring requirements, reporting obligations, and noncompliance notification requirements under the Clean Water Act, 40 CFR Part 122, and federal pretreatment requirements under 40 CFR Part 403, and applicable state or local regulatory programs.
- 7+ years of experience developing or implementing water-quality sampling and monitoring programs, including sampling plans, sampling locations, analytical parameters and methods, sampling equipment, laboratory coordination, and data evaluation.
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings

Preferred qualifications

- Experience supporting water compliance across multiple facilities, jurisdictions, or regulatory programs, and with public water system requirements under the Safe Drinking Water Act, 40 CFR Part 141, and applicable state drinking-water programs.
- Working knowledge of potable water and septic/onsite wastewater treatment systems, including their design, operation, monitoring, and regulatory compliance.
- Experience with industrial wastewater treatment, pretreatment systems, publicly owned treatment works, and local industrial-user permits, including evaluating the design and operation of water and wastewater treatment, conveyance, storage, sampling, and monitoring systems.
- Experience reviewing civil, mechanical, plumbing, and process designs for water-related regulatory and permit compliance.
- Experience developing scalable environmental standards, procedures, tools, or compliance mechanisms for use across multiple sites, and managing multiple technically complex projects and regulatory deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

title: Energy Analytics, TPM, Global Energy, Sustainability and Automation
descriptionHtml:
The Energy Analytics, Technical Program Manager (TPM) will scale power monitoring, insight generation, and energy and carbon reduction initiatives across Amazon's North America fulfillment operations. In this hands-on technical role, you will deploy and generate analysis from power metering infrastructure and implement load flexibility and energy optimization roadmaps that deliver measurable cost savings and carbon reductions. This work directly supports Amazon's demand-side power requirements and Climate Pledge commitments.

You will operate as an individual contributor, owning the delivery of defined and ambiguous work-streams while partnering with engineering, controls, data, operations and deployment teams to implement changes. You will influence cross-functional partners without authority, primarily at the team and management level, using data to drive decisions. You will integrate and analyze power metering information, providing load forecasts and generating cost and energy savings opportunities. Utility rate structures, time of day, demand ratchets and power factor penalties will influence your strategies. Technical assets influenced can include material handling, robotics, powered industrial trucks, lighting, heating ventilation and air conditioning, plug loads, electrical metering and more. Developed projects will be scaled across hundreds of facilities across the network, producing energy, cost and carbon benefit.

Key job responsibilities
● Build and execute technical solutions for energy and carbon reduction from pilot, data collection, through scaled implementation and measurement & verification (M&V) of results.  Energy and load optimization via control systems is a technical requirement: energy-conservation/standby modes, variable speed applications, and equipment scheduling.
● Drive continuous monitoring and energy efficiency improvements with Amazon's energy consuming assets.  Integrate power metering into our data sets, and develop analytics to identify opportunities, assess trending consumption changes, and measure benefits of conservation efforts.
● Prepare written analysis of feasibility studies and recommendations for various energy monitoring and power flexibility strategies.  Own metering data quality programs, check readings for completeness, outliers, and flag actionable improvements, and reconcile against known loads to ensure trusted insight generation.
● Develop metrics, baselines, and roadmaps that translate technical work into quantified outcomes (energy savings, cost savings or utility tariff arbitrage, load forecast, reliability, carbon reduction).
● Define and own technical approach and cross-system architecture for data configuration, standards and mechanisms for scalability and enforcement of key energy savings mechanisms. Decide how to build and prove new approaches managing tradeoffs for necessary business needs, rather than executing a defined scope.
● Manage projects against plans and objectives to ensure commitments are met, delivering against our power and Climate Pledge goals.
● Deep diving (troubleshooting) and unblocking issues that are prohibiting teams from pursuing energy reduction initiatives.
● Work with critical stakeholders on developing mechanisms for design standard integration for launching facilities that incorporate energy optimization procedures from Day 1.
● Analyze and communicate the financial impact of projects and initiatives (payback, return on investment, net present value)
● Serve as a technical reviewer for peers and partner engineers — reviewing control logic, metering architecture, and design-standard changes, and improving them on technical merit
● Quantify and own value add of energy savings mechanisms and how they reduce equipment runtime and increases reliability and lifespan.
● Calculate and report energy, water and carbon savings using International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol methodologies.
● Manage multiple, complex projects simultaneously.
● Produce clear documentation, playbooks, and reporting that make work-streams repeatable.

A day in the life
You might spend the morning querying newly integrated power-metering data and validating it against the distribution-panel hierarchy — resolving a data-quality gap — then analyzing load profiles and build an energy-savings or peak-shaving model that quantifies the opportunity by equipment class. You then define network rollout suitability and prioritize these opportunities across sites. In the afternoon you develop control logic changes to implement an efficiency opportunity, propose updates to a design standard, or define a measurement method for implemented energy and cost savings to your stakeholders. You balance trade-offs between energy savings, technical complexity, equipment reliability, and cost — bringing well-reasoned recommendations and escalating the most ambiguous decisions for alignment.

About the team
The Global Energy, Sustainability and Automation (GESA) Energy team is dedicated to delivering energy efficiency, cost savings, and demand flexibility within Amazon's fulfillment network. We partner closely with design, controls, data, procurement, operations, field engineering, and deployment teams — as well as external vendors — to ensure our energy consumption is monitored and optimized. Our focus in the coming years is scaling our energy monitoring and analytics programs, expanding behavioral and retrofit programs, expanding load flexibility for power resilience and cost arbitrage benefit, and enhancing asset reliability and lifespan through efficient operation. If you are energized by large-scale technical challenges and want to make a tangible impact on energy use, this is the team for you.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
- Experience in SQL Server/MySQL, or experience in Redshift and experience in any Bigdata architecture
- Experience working with existing and emerging technologies related to building energy (i.e. power metering, conveyance, robotics, controls, HVAC, charging infrastructure)

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing cross-functional programs and release schedules
- Familiarity with automation engineering and controls engineering concepts.
- Industry certifications: Certified Energy Manager, Certified Measurement & Verification Professional, Professional Engineer.

title: EHS Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. As a Workplace Health & Safety Specialist (WHSS), you'll be at the forefront of transforming workplace safety culture at one of the world's most innovative companies. Your expertise and dedication will directly protect employees, ensuring they return home safely to their families every day. You'll facilitate new approaches to safety, combining technology with human-centered solutions to create an environment where safety and productivity thrive together. This isn't just about maintaining safety standards – it's about revolutionizing how we think about and implement workplace safety, making a lasting impact on our people and operations. As your building's designated safety champion, you'll have the unique opportunity to build relationships, influence positive change, and help write the next chapter in Amazon's commitment to becoming Earth's Safest Place to Work.

Core Impact Areas:
Safety Program Excellence & Implementation - Drive comprehensive safety programs through data-driven strategies. Lead daily safety audits, incident investigations, and risk assessments while implementing innovative solutions to prevent injuries. Deliver engaging safety training that resonates with associates and promotes a proactive safety culture. Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance workplace safety while maintaining operational efficiency.

Associate Advocacy & Cultural Leadership - Serve as a trusted safety advisor and advocate for associate wellbeing, building strong partnerships across all levels of the organization. Foster a culture where safety is everyone's priority through effective communication, coaching, and positive reinforcement. Develop strong relationships with frontline associates and leadership to drive behavioral changes and ensure safety best practices become natural habits. Transform safety data into compelling narratives that influence positive change and drive engagement in safety initiatives.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site

Must be available to work flexible shifts including days, nights and/or weekends.

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent
- A minimum of 1 year in an Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) related field OR; A Bachelor’s degree in EHS-relevant background OR; 6 months experience performing in a safety-related role within Amazon
- Knowledge of OSHA regulations specifically 29 CFR 1910
- Experience using Microsoft Word and Excel in a professional capacity
- Experience maintaining confidentiality in matter involving security and/or personnel issues in the workplace

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or higher, preferably in a safety related field
- Strong communication, teamwork, analysis, judgment, and customer focus skills
- Experience leading and managing a team, ability to analyze accident data, new processes, and machinery for potential safety concerns, and conduct job hazard and job safety analyses
- Experience in emergency response and currently holds First Aid and CPR certificates
- Experience in workers compensation case management

title: Principal Applied Scientist, AWS Data Center Services
descriptionHtml:
Application deadline: Nov 16, 2026

The AWS Data Center Services team is hiring a Principal Applied Scientist to innovate and advance the science behind solutions to problems in the rapidly growing AWS data center space.

These problems range from bespoke computer vision models to support our physical infrastructure functions such as repair activities, to increasing the certainty of decisions made by our generative AI service without sacrificing latency or performance. For example, when a data center technician is triaging a critical electrical event at 2am and alarms cascade in seconds, our AI service has to cross-reference topology, live readings, maintenance history, and design documents within minutes - work that today takes an order of magnitude more time and intervention from a senior engineer.

As a Principal Applied Scientist, you will work backwards from these problems and partner with software development teams to deliver solutions. You will work on problems ranging from selecting, training and evolving computer vision models for targeted activities on AWS infrastructure inside our data centers; to building smart retrieval algorithms, reduce model hallucination on safety-critical outcomes, continually improve latency and performance, and ensure our generative AI service's knowledgeable stays current and the service is constantly getting smarter beyond just knowledge retrieval.

A day in the life
You start the morning reviewing traces from last night’s incident triage. The agent correctly walked the topology to the upstream breaker but missed a recent maintenance change that was the real cause — so you design an experiment: does feeding work-order history into the traversal improve accuracy? You test it against historical incident data. Mid-morning, you review verification traces and catch the agent missing a spec deep in a submittal. After lunch, a field engineer walks you through manually cross-referencing five systems during an incident and you turn their scenario into a new benchmark. In the afternoon, you prototype cross-discipline reasoning: when a cascade spans electrical and cooling, can the lead agent delegate scoped investigations and still hold one coherent hypothesis? You publish results and draft a paper. You own the full lifecycle — research through production deployment.

About the team
Data Center Services is part of AWS Infrastructure Services that owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain - and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

title: Infrastructure Partner Management Intern, AWS Infrastructure Services
descriptionHtml:
Internship period : 4 Jan 2027 - 30 June 2027

Amazon Web Services (AWS) · APAC — Data Center Supply Solutions · 6-month placement
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on challenging problems with thousands of variables — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.
You'll join a diverse team of supply chain specialists, operations managers, security and engineering experts, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them.
About the Infrastructure Partner Management (IPM) team
AWS doesn't only run its own data centers. It also places infrastructure inside data centers owned and operated by external providers — known as "colocation" partners. The IPM team manages these partnerships from the AWS side, across the whole life of a site, from the day a contract is signed to the day the site is closed.
We are the bridge between the AWS teams who run the data centers and the partners who host them. We work to make sure both sides deliver on what was agreed, and that the partnership runs smoothly day to day. We measure performance against agreed service levels (SLAs) so that it's transparent and objective for everyone, and when challenges come up we help bring the right people together to resolve them. Above all, we invest in strong, trusted relationships — understanding how each partner operates, working through problems together, and finding solutions that work for both sides, so our shared customers can depend on the infrastructure.
The work falls into a few repeating cycles:

* Business reviews. We run a regular Colocation Business Review (CBR) program — scheduled meetings with each partner to review performance against agreed service levels (SLAs) and align on actions together.
* Relationship management. We build long-term, trusted relationships with each partner — understanding how they operate, working through challenges together, and finding the win-win — so the partnership stays healthy well beyond any single review.
* Performance tracking. Between reviews, we track service levels, open action items, and follow through to resolution.
* Issue resolution. When a challenge comes up between AWS teams and a partner, we help bring the right people together and work it through.
* Commercial oversight. We manage our colocation contracts so that all parties are clear on their commitments and delivering against them.
* Continuous improvement. We keep reviewing our own ways of working and build better processes — including automation — so the team runs more efficiently over time.

This is not a hands-on engineering or on-site operations job. It's about working with data, supporting partner reviews, and learning how AWS manages and strengthens its colocation partnerships.
About the role
This 6-month placement supports the IPM team. You won't own a partner portfolio on your own — you'll work alongside experienced Infrastructure Partner Managers, take on well-defined pieces of real work, and always have an IPM close by to guide and review what you produce.
No two days look the same, but a typical one pulls from the cycles above. You might spend the morning preparing for a partner business review — pulling service-level data into the review pack — then sit in on the review itself to see how the partnership is managed in practice. The afternoon might turn to data: tidying up an export, spotting a trend across a few sites, and writing a line on what it tells us. Along the way you'll help keep our records up to date, follow up on open actions, and make progress on your own improvement project with your mentor. The throughline is simple — you're supporting and learning, not owning the partner relationships.


Key job responsibilities
Supporting business reviews

* Help set up and prepare Colocation Business Reviews (CBRs) — building the data packs, pulling service-level numbers, and drafting the summary slides the IPM presents
* Sit in on reviews to learn how the partnerships are managed, and capture the actions that come out of them
* Help draft one-pagers — short summary documents for a business review or a specific topic — pulling the facts together for an IPM to review and finalise
* Help develop automation that supports the team's business reviews

Tracking and follow-up

* Help keep action items and open topics up to date in our tracking systems, and follow up so nothing slips
* Track service-level performance across sites and partners, and surface anything that needs an IPM's attention

Commercial and data/AI work

* Help build and maintain simple trackers, contract/obligation lists, and dashboards
* Pull and clean data, surfacing insights or trends the team can take clear, objective action on

Learning the wider role

* Work with AWS teams — Safety, Security, Operations, Engineering, Finance, and Business Development — to see how the partnerships are managed day to day
* Sit in on partner conversations beyond the formal reviews, and see how IPMs build trust and work through challenges collaboratively
* Support one process-improvement or automation project end to end, with a defined outcome and a mentor

title: Applied Scientist, Agentic AI, AWS Governance
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to build the ML models that power every compliance verdict customers and auditors rely on? We are building a new Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) service at AWS where every action — human or agent — is recorded, assessed, and provably governed, continuously and at any scale.

As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will own the Natural Language Inference (NLI) model at the center of our compliance engine: fine-tuning, calibrating, and monitoring it in production. You will also design the science behind framework decomposition, evidence auto-linking, and a new agent-context system that tackles retrieval, grounding, and hallucination measurement for AI agents. Your work will directly shape the accuracy and trustworthiness of every customer-visible result we produce.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the production NLI model end-to-end: fine-tune, promote, calibrate thresholds, and monitor for drift to ensure accurate compliance verdicts across frameworks.
- Design and implement framework decomposition pipelines that translate compliance controls into NLI hypotheses, including enrichment and per-framework threshold calibration.
- Build and improve the evidence auto-linking system using ranking, embedding, and reranking techniques, tuning precision-recall tradeoffs and addressing OCR quality challenges.
- Drive the quality flywheel by establishing labeling standards, designing offline and online evaluation methods, orchestrating retraining cycles, and ensuring privacy-safe data handling.
- Research and develop the agent-context capability — retrieval and representation of lifecycle signals, cross-framework knowledge, memory, grounding, and hallucination measurement — collaborating with engineering pods to bring these models into production.

A day in the life
You will split your time between collaborative and heads-down work. On the collaborative side, you will partner with several pods of software development engineers in an Agile cadence — aligning on data collection needs, sharing experiment results, and integrating models into production services. On the heads-down side, you will dig into model training runs, analyze evaluation metrics, and iterate on threshold tuning until the numbers meet the bar. Your work is roadmap-driven, giving you the space to plan experiments methodically while still responding to new framework onboarding requests as they arise.

About the team
Our team builds the AI and ML systems behind AWS Governance, Risk, & Compliance service, where science is not auxiliary — it is the core. Every customer-visible compliance result flows through models our scientists create and maintain. We are investing in next-generation capabilities including observability and governance for AI agents, and the multi-quarter Agent Context initiative is an organization-defining program that will need technical leaders.

Growth here is tangible. You will own the full model lifecycle from training through production monitoring, develop rare expertise at the intersection of ML and compliance, and have a clear path to expand your scope into technical leadership as the service scales.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of building models for business application experience
- 2+ years of programming in Java, C++, Python or related language experience
- 2+ years of hands-on predictive modeling and large data analysis experience

Preferred qualifications

- PhD in computer science, machine learning, engineering, or related fields
- Experience in written and verbal communication with the ability to present complex technical information in a clear and concise manner to executives and non-technical leaders
- Experience with one of the following areas: machine learning technologies, Reinforcement Learning, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing (NLP) or related applications
- Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing
- Extensive experience applying theoretical models in an applied environment.
- Experience with building agentic systems using LLMs and familiar with common agentic framework such as Strands Agent, LangGraph, etc.
- Solid knowledge on LLM techniques and experience with LLM post-training.

title: Program Manager, FSOE PM, JCFS
descriptionHtml:
オペレーション技術統括本部（英語名称JCFS: Japan Customer Fulfillment Solutions）はアマゾンジャパン オペレーション部門（JP Ops）の中核部門として、物流プロセスの設計・導入・改善に取り組むとともに、物流プロセスのベースとなる建屋の設計を最適化して、拠点の価値を最大化することに注力しています。

アマゾンジャパンは、商品をお客様に迅速に届けるための大規模拠点の立ち上げをリードするプロジェクトマネジメントをおこなうとともに、今までにない新しい建屋・設備に関するイノベーションやソリューションを生み出すことで、拠点の価値を最大化する活動を推進するSr Program Managerを探しています。
このポジションは、Amazon拠点の新規工事や改修工事のプロジェクトにおいて、社内ステークホルダーと連携してマスタープランの作成、予算管理、リスク管理をリードするプロジェクトマネジメントの役割を担います。そして、そのような下流の仕事に加え、政府や自治体といった法律や規制を司る社外ステークホルダーとネットワークを構築し、今までにない新しい建屋・設備に関するソリューションを生み出すことで、長期的にアマゾン拠点のコスト構造を改善していく上流のプログラムマネジメントの役割も担います。そのため、このポジションには、建屋・設備に関するプロジェクトの上流から下流までの幅広いフェーズにおいて、リーダーシップを発揮し、技術的視点で問題解決や改善提案を実行できる能力と経験が求められます。また、国内外ステークホルダーと電話会議や対面で業務依頼、交渉をするため日本語、英語によるコミュニケーション能力、プロジェクトメンバーとの定例会議におけるファシリテーション能力、プロジェクト進捗レポート作成のためのドキュメンテーション能力も必要です。

Amazonでは、最新のAI Tool, 生成AIを日々の業務の中に積極的に取り入れています。
AI Toolは私たちの意思決定のスピードを加速させ、私たちを本当に重要な「判断」と「議論」に集中させることを可能にしています。Amazon では学習を継続する文化が根付いているため、ご自身のペースでAIに関する知識を深めることができるリソースが用意されています。


Key job responsibilities
-政府・自治体・業界団体といった社外ステークホルダーとのネットワーク・信頼関係を構築し、規制緩和・法改正の実現に向けた折衝・交渉をリードする。
-アマゾン拠点の新規工事や改修工事のプロジェクトマネージャーとして、スケジュールや予算のプランニングをおこない、実行段階において進捗管理とリスク管理をおこなう。
-規制・行政手続きに関わる課題を特定し、解決に向けた中長期のプログラムマネジメントをおこない、実現可能性の検証から施策の実行・定着までをリードする。
-拠点の安定したオペレーション体制を脅かすリスク（行政・近隣・法規制に起因するものを含む）を早期に特定・評価し、リスク低減に向けた関係者調整と対応策の立案・実行をおこなう。
-行政・自治体・近隣との折衝プロセスにおいて、社内ステークホルダー（経営層・法務・広報・オペレーション等）と連携し、組織横断的な対応体制を構築・維持する。


A day in the life
毎週のチームミーティングで、各メンバーの進捗や成果、優先する取り組み、サポートが必要な内容を確認しながら業務をおこないます。業務を進めるうえで何か迷うことがあれば、チャット、ビデオ通話、F2Fの会話を通して気軽に相談しながら、チーム全体でサポートし合います。フレックスが基本ですが、原則18時以降は会議やメールは行いません。有給消化率も高く長期休暇も、もちろん取得可能です。

About the team
アマゾンジャパンオペレーションのエンジニアリング部門として、大規模拠点の立ち上げや建屋・設備の改善によって、アマゾンジャパンの成長に直接影響を与える事ができます。そして、政府や自治体といった社外ステークホルダーとネットワークを構築し、法改正や規制緩和をおこなうことで、革新的なソリューションを生み出すダイナミックな活動をおこないます。また、社内経営層はじめJCFS各チームやファイナンス、調達部門等、様々なステークホルダーとの協業が必要なポジションです。海外のチームとも交流を持ち、相互のベストプラクティスの横展開を積極的に推進する事でアマゾン、アマゾンジャパン並びに自分自身の成長に繋げる事ができます。入社後はチーム全体で既存プロセス・知識の共有、トレーニング、日々の面談を行い、オンボーディングをサポートします。

Basic qualifications

- 大学の学士 または工学の修士号
- 政府や自治体を巻き込んだ渉外折衝業務に従事した経験
- 建設プロジェクトや新規ビジネスの立ち上げにおける 5年以上のリーダーシップおよびプロジェクト管理の経験

title: Human Resources Business Partner , Worldwide Grocery Stores
descriptionHtml:
This role supports Whole Foods Market stores, within the Worldwide Grocery Stores organization.

Amazon is seeking a strategic and solution-focused Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP) to power the trajectory of our business by ensuring we have the right talent mix, leadership, and capabilities to innovate and deliver exceptional customer and Team Member experiences. As an HRBP, you will serve as a leader of people and organizational strategy — accelerating business outcomes through diagnosis, development, and execution of integrated solutions.

You will build trusted relationships with leaders and act as the client face of TMS (Team Member Services), interfacing and liaising with Recruiting, Team Member / Team Leader Development, Compensation, Benefits, HRIS, and the Legal organization. You will coach, act as a change agent, and influence critical decisions around talent and organizational design to drive business results while ensuring compliance with corporate policies, government regulations, and statutory requirements.

This role requires travel up to 25% of the time.


Key job responsibilities
Organizational Effectiveness

Leverage deep knowledge of the business — including P&L, retail operations, and the competitive grocery/retail landscape — to tailor people-focused solutions that drive business outcomes

Interpret key people metrics and trends, utilizing mechanisms to inspect, monitor, and proactively mitigate organizational risks

Design, recommend, and implement effective organizational structures that align with business strategy, strengthen culture, and enable inclusive decision-making

Partner with leaders to build customer-centric, Team Member–focused organizations that foster agility and empower frontline decision-making

Ensure dynamic assessment of organizational capability — strengths, weaknesses, and opportunities — on a forward-looking basis

Recommend new approaches, policies, and procedures to drive continual improvement in TMS service delivery

Leader and Leadership Team Effectiveness

Assess both long-term and immediate leader talent needs to achieve business goals

Develop strategies to build required leader skills and establish inclusive talent pipelines

Coach and advise individual leaders and leadership teams on improving management abilities, addressing business challenges, and strengthening culture

Challenge leaders when necessary to break mental models on ways of working, biases, structure, and talent decisions

Reinforce difficult decisions that align with organizational strategies and values

Change Management

Use listening mechanisms to identify trends, risks, and hotspots to inform change plans and maximize both customer and Team Member experience

Drive effective change environments by leveraging multiple perspectives and inclusive communication strategies

Influence and coach leaders as they build their teams' ability to navigate organizational changes

Monitor and evaluate implemented changes to assess effectiveness and durability

Talent Planning & Workforce Strategy

Build long-term, inclusive workforce plans aligned with business objectives; proactively identify current and anticipated workforce capability gaps and develop strategies to close them

Coach and support leaders in executing workforce plans and making resource-allocation decisions

Anticipate industry trends and talent needs, determining gaps in current and future capabilities

Create talent goals and cadence with the Leadership Team, building inclusive talent mechanisms into the organization's rhythm of business

Team Member Relations & Compliance

Consult with and advise organizational leaders and Team Members on TM relations and related issues within assigned client groups

Provide sound policy interpretations and practice decisions; ensure adherence to company policies and applicable federal, state, and local regulations (including FMLA, ADA, HIPAA, and Leaves of Absence)

Provide assigned client teams and leaders with training, coaching, and guidance to maintain compliance

Serve as a neutral, approachable TMS professional who recognizes and proactively resolves potential people and organizational issues — escalating as appropriate

A day in the life
This is an in-person role. You’ll be on-site in our stores four days per week, working shoulder-to-shoulder with the leaders and Team Members you support — walking the floor and being a familiar, trusted face, not working from behind a desk or screen.
This role requires balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You will partner with business leaders to develop HR solutions aligned with business objectives, support organizational design initiatives, drive talent strategies, and create mechanisms to assess organizational health. You must be comfortable dealing with ambiguity while building structured approaches to drive successful and equitable outcomes.
The HRBP serves as a trusted advisor and member of the business leadership team — expected to bring perspectives on the intersections of people strategy and business performance. You will engage as a subject matter expert on TMS-related topics and model a commitment to customer service, Team Member well-being, and the values that set our organization apart.
The best HRBPs in our stores are the ones leaders and Team Members know by name — approachable in the aisle and the break room, not just in meetings. Strategy matters, but only when it’s grounded in real understanding of the people doing the work every day.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of HR work within an international, fast-paced, and customer-driven environment experience
- 2+ years of human resources or a mix of equivalent experience
- 2+ years of human resources or equivalent (e.g., operations, customer service, retail, distribution, shipping/logistics, healthcare, hospitality, manufacturing) experience
- Knowledge of local labor law
- Experience in HR within an international, fast-paced and customer-driven environment
- Experience in a call center, distribution center, or manufacturing environment
- Experience supporting hourly employee client group
- Experience with MS Office tools and HR Information Systems
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- 3+ years of HR experience
- Experience with HR processes and systems
- Experience with analytical tools and ability to dive deep into metrics and reporting
- 4+ years of retail or operations, or 4+ years of customer-facing retail, hospitality, or grocery industry experience
- Experience supporting or leading employee-focused processes including onboarding, benefits, investigations, training or talent management
- • Willingness to work on-site four days per week, including time on the sales floor

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Human Resources Management
- Experience in human resources with companies supporting 250-500 or more associates
- Experience managing and leading employees
- Master's degree or above in Human Resources Management, Business Administration or a related field
- Experience in e-commerce, retail or advertising, or experience communicating with a wide range of stakeholders, including colleagues and leadership
- Experience in retail, operations and/or business management
- Experience analyzing HR metrics and using data insights to drive business decisions
- Experience handling ambiguous or undefined challenges through strong problem solving abilities
- Experience hiring and developing strong talent and building a team
- Knowledge of retail food code and regulations governing grocery retail at local, state, and federal levels

title: IMDb Policy Manager, IMDb
descriptionHtml:
IMDb is the world's most popular source for movie, TV, and celebrity content, reaching an audience of more than 250 million unique visitors per month. We're looking for a Senior Policy Program Manager to join IMDb's Content Operations team and own the full lifecycle of content policy — from creation and versioning through to enforcement and machine-interpretability.

In this role, you'll be the dedicated owner of IMDb's policy framework, ensuring that our policies are clearly authored, properly versioned, consistently enforced, and structured for machine consumption by our automated moderation systems. You'll define and maintain the policy store and tag definitions that power IMDb's multi-layered moderation architecture. This role requires someone who can navigate ambiguity, drive cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, Legal, PR, and Operations, and deliver measurable improvements to policy coverage and enforcement accuracy at scale.

The most successful candidate will think strategically about how policy decisions impact hundreds of millions of users, while diving deep into the technical details of how policies are codified and interpreted by automated systems.

Key job responsibilities
• Own end-to-end policy creation, versioning and publication across IMDb's content ecosystem, managing the full lifecycle from identification of need through stakeholder sign-off to implementation.
• Design and maintain the policy store authoring framework and tags that enables policies to be machine-readable and enforceable by automated moderation systems.
• Drive cross-functional collaboration with Product Management, Engineering, Legal, PR, Risk Management, and Operations to ensure policies are comprehensive, compliant, and implementable.
• Define program strategy for policy governance, including prioritization frameworks, SLA tracking, and metrics to measure policy effectiveness and enforcement accuracy.
• Present policy risks, recommendations, and program updates to Directors and VPs, building consensus across discordant views and securing resources for policy initiatives.
• Identify and drive process improvements to streamline policy workflows, reduce time-to-enforcement, and eliminate redundant or conflicting policies across the organization.
• Identify new trends in the entertainment industry and develop new policies to support them.

A day in the life
You'll start your day reviewing policy effectiveness metrics and enforcement signals, identifying where gaps or inconsistencies exist between policy intent and automated enforcement. You might spend the morning drafting a new policy in response to an emerging content challenge, working through the stakeholder review process with Legal and PR. In the afternoon, you could be partnering with Engineering to refine how a policy is codified for machine interpretation, ensuring the tag definitions and rule configurations accurately reflect the policy's intent. You'll regularly present to senior leadership on policy program health, upcoming changes, and strategic direction.

Basic qualifications

- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience in program or project management
- Experience using data and metrics to drive improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
- Knowledge of general AI tools

Preferred qualifications

- Experience leading process improvements

title: Benefits Manager, Global Retirement and Investments Team (GRIT)
descriptionHtml:
​​Amazon's Global Retirement & Investments team is looking for a Benefits Manager to oversee the end-to-end management of retirement benefits across multiple international jurisdictions. You will own the design, governance, operational management, and continuous improvement of pension and retirement schemes that serve many thousands of Amazon employees, partnering with trustees, providers, investment advisors, payroll, HR, finance, legal, and benefits teams to ensure these programs run smoothly and deliver a strong employee experience. You will also develop and maintain risk management frameworks that protect plan integrity, monitor regulatory developments across your assigned jurisdictions, and drive operational excellence through data-driven reporting and process improvement. This high-impact role combines strategic benefits management with hands-on oversight, sitting at the intersection of employee experience, ongoing management, compliance, and corporate and plan governance.​

Key job responsibilities
- Oversee the end-to-end administration and governance of retirement programs across assigned markets (e.g., UK pension schemes), partnering with trustees, investment advisors, and third-party administrators to deliver well-run plans and a positive member experience.
- Lead investment oversight for your portfolio — fund-lineup monitoring, performance review against benchmarks, and preparation of investment-governance materials.
- Lead vendor reviews, RFPs, and plan-design benchmarking; manage plan and vendor costs against budget, delivering savings through fee negotiation and confirming value for money.
- Monitor regulatory developments from local pension authorities (e.g., The Pensions Regulator), conduct compliance assessments (e.g., UK auto-enrolment), and manage cyclical governance activities to keep programs compliant.
- Coordinate with payroll, HR, finance, legal, compliance, and benefits teams to ensure seamless data flows, accurate reporting, and timely issue resolution.
- Own member-facing retirement content and communications — deliver annual campaigns and drive participation against enrollment and satisfaction targets; build data-driven dashboards and papers for governance committees and leadership reviews.
- Support expansion into new international markets, and contribute to broader Global Retirement & Investments initiatives and cross-country governance standards.

A day in the life
​​Your day might begin by reviewing retirement program operations across your assigned markets — checking enrollment data, contribution accuracy, and flagging any issues for resolution with payroll or your third-party administrators. Mid-morning, you could be joining a call with trustees or investment advisors to discuss plan governance or upcoming regulatory changes in one of your jurisdictions. After lunch, you might shift to analyzing plan performance data and updating dashboards that track operational health and risk indicators, before connecting with HR and benefits colleagues on employee queries or upcoming compliance cycles. No two days are the same — you will move between hands-on operational oversight, stakeholder collaboration, and longer-term strategic work like process improvements or supporting the expansion of retirement programs into new international markets.​

About the team
Sitting within Amazon's broader Benefits organization, the Global Retirement & Investments team is a collaborative group of retirement and benefits professionals committed to delivering exceptional employee experiences through well-designed, well-run pension and retirement benefits. Our vision is to build scalable, compliant retirement programs that serve Amazon employees across multiple countries and adapt to evolving regulatory landscapes. We work across geographies and business units — partnering with HR, benefits, compensation, technology, payroll, and operations teams — to ensure our programs remain employee-focused, operationally sound, and compliant. We're excited to welcome someone who shares our commitment to excellence and understands the importance of protecting our employees' retirement security.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, or a related field
- Experience managing pension or retirement benefits programs, including scheme administration, governance, design, and vendors.
- ​​Knowledge of pension or retirement plan frameworks in at least one major market (e.g., UK auto-enrolment, defined contribution/defined benefit structures)
- Experience coordinating with multiple stakeholders such as trustees, advisors, payroll, and HR teams
- Experience managing concurrent workstreams such as implementations, vendor transitions, and regulatory projects, managing competing deadlines, dependencies, and stakeholders.

Preferred qualifications

- ​​Professional pension or benefits certification (e.g., PMI, IIPM, CFA, or local equivalent)​
- ​​Experience with a variety of retirement plan structures across different markets (e.g., UK master trusts, defined benefit schemes, or equivalent international programs)​
- Managing and influencing senior stakeholders, including trustee boards.
- Experience building or improving operational processes, reporting frameworks, or benefits program governance
- Familiarity with risk management principles as applied to pension or benefits programs
- Experience working across multiple countries or jurisdictions on retirement or benefits programs
- Comfort with data visualization tools or analytics platforms for operational reporting; interpreting benefit data and applying critical judgment skills to inform design, operational and governance decisions.
